Plan below is a safe, coach-friendly 1RM testing protocol to be performed at the end of Phase 3 (Week 12 active-deload) to assess progress on the primary strength lifts (back squat, bench press, deadlift, and optionally overhead press). Because Week 12 is an active deload in the program, testing should be scheduled on a day when fatigue is lowest (not the same day as a plyo/HIIT session). I recommend scheduling testing on the Monday or Tuesday of Week 12 depending on how your client feels — ideally after 48+ hours easy recovery (for example: rest Sun, test Mon). Use the protocol below, prioritize safety and technical quality, and record loads, reps and RPE.

Overview and safety considerations
- Tested lifts: Back squat, Bench press, Deadlift. Optionally test Overhead press if you want an additional data point.
- Timing: Test during Week 12 but pick a single day if you can (split into two days if necessary for recovery). Recommended order if testing in one day: Bench press → Overhead press (optional) → Back squat → Deadlift. If two days, do upper body on Day 1 and lower body on Day 2.
- Rest: Allow full recovery between maximal attempts—3–5 min between ramp sets, 4–6+ min between 1RM attempts. If doing multiple exercises in one day, allow 10–15 min between heavy lift types (upper → lower).
- Spotters and safety: Use spotters for bench and squat; use a power rack with safety pins. Belt and appropriate footwear recommended. Stop if technique breaks down or if any sharp pain occurs.
- Warm-up: Progressive and specific. Ramp up gradually with sets of increasing load and decreasing reps (see detailed warm-up below).

Pre-test checklist (48–72 hours beforehand)
- Reduce training volume the two days prior (light activity only, mobility). In Week 12 active-deload this should already be in place.
- Prioritize sleep 8+ hours and normal carbohydrate intake the day before.
- Hydrate well and have a small carb-rich meal 60–90 minutes before testing (e.g., toast + banana + yogurt).
- Creatine: continue daily if already using.
- Avoid heavy cardio the day before.

Test day protocol (one-day full test; split into two days if preferred)

General warm-up (10–15 min)
- 5–7 min easy aerobic (bike/row) to increase body temperature
- Mobility and movement prep (hips, thoracic, shoulders)
- Dynamic activations (glute bridges, band pull-aparts, bodyweight squats, lunges)

Lift-specific ramp (examples — adjust weights based on estimated working max)
- Bench press warm-up ramp (example if estimated 1RM ~80 kg):
  - Bar x 10–15 reps (empty bar)
  - 40% of estimated 1RM x 5
  - 60% x 3
  - 75% x 2
  - 85% x 1
  - Rest 2–3 min, then begin 1RM attempts
- Back squat warm-up ramp (example if estimated 1RM ~120 kg):
  - Bodyweight or empty bar x 8–10
  - 40% x 5
  - 60% x 3
  - 75% x 2
  - 85% x 1
  - Rest 2–3 min, then 1RM attempts
- Deadlift warm-up ramp (example if estimated 1RM ~150 kg):
  - Trap-bar/empty bar x 5–8 (if using trap)
  - 40% x 5
  - 60% x 3
  - 75% x 2
  - 85% x 1
  - Rest 2–3 min, then 1RM attempts

1RM attempt strategy (per lift)
- After warm-up ramp, take 2–4 maximal attempts total per lift (include only as many as needed to find true 1RM). Increase load by ~2.5–5% (upper body) or ~2.5–5–10% (lower body) between attempts depending on how close to true max you are.
- If you hit the attempt with good technique and it feels like you could do 1 more rep, increase by the smaller increment for the next attempt.
- If the attempt is missed, reduce by ~2–5% and try again after full rest only if form is safe and the lifter feels ready.
- Use RPE as a guide—stops when technique degrades or the lifter indicates RPE 10 (maximal).

Suggested attempt progression example (bench)
- After ramp to 85% x1: Attempt 1 = 92–94% x1, if good Attempt 2 = 97–99% or 100+% x1. Adjust based on feel.
- For squat/deadlift: after 85% ramp, try 92–95% as first max attempt, then 97–101% if successful.

Order and single-day time management
- If testing all three in one day, start with upper-body lifts (bench) to minimize lower-body fatigue before squat/deadlift. Recommended order: Bench → Overhead press (optional) → Back squat → Deadlift. Expect total testing session to take 90–150 minutes depending on rests and number of attempts.
- If two-day split: Day 1 (Bench ± OHP); Day 2 (Squat + Deadlift). Split is less fatiguing and often yields cleaner 1RMs.

Recording & logging
- Record the following for each attempt: weight, number of attempts, success/fail, rep speed (bar speed if available), technical notes, and RPE.
- Take video if possible (coach angle) for technical review and to validate lifts.

Testing environment and coaching cues
- Warm room, supportive footwear, appropriate lifting belt if used in training.
- Coach gives consistent cues and counts: tight setup, bracing, controlled descent (bench/squat) and explosive concentric. For deadlift cue: set back neutral, start with leg drive, lockout with hips.
- Use power rack safeties and spotters for bench and squat.

Post-test recovery
- Light cool-down and mobility after testing.
- Post-test meal: 20–40 g protein + 40–80 g carbohydrates to replenish and support recovery.
- Avoid heavy training for at least 3–4 days after testing (this aligns with Week 12 active-deload). Use the remainder of Week 12 for technique work, mobility, and active recovery.

Interpreting results and next steps
- Compare 1RM results to baseline (if you have starting values) to quantify strength changes. Useful metrics:
  - Absolute 1RM change (kg)
  - Percent change ((end 1RM − start 1RM) / start 1RM ×100)
  - Relative strength (1RM/bodyweight) if bodyweight tracked
- Use results to inform next training block: if lifts increased substantially (desired), plan next block with new percentages and progressive overload. If progress is limited, audit training logs, nutrition adherence, recovery and consider adjusting volume/intensity or implementing an accumulation block.
- If you want, I can convert the new 1RMs into a % progression for the next 12-week block or provide suggestions (e.g., a 6–8 week accumulation block or a repeat of the program with adjusted loads).

- Day 1 (Mon): Upper 1RM test — Bench press 1RM; optional Overhead press 1RM. Finish with light mobility and an easy protein-rich meal.
- Day 2 (Tue): Lower 1RM test — Back squat 1RM; Rest 10–15 min; Deadlift 1RM. Finish with recovery nutrition and mobility.
- Wed–Sun: Active recovery, mobility, minimal low-intensity cardio only.
